Published online:
    September 11, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — references July CPI, August PPI, August employment data
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Fed September 15-16 meeting, November midterms, August CPI release imminent
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    U.S. CPI for August is expected to accelerate to +0.4% MoM / +3.4% YoY, driven by a gasoline rebound above $4.19/gallon and oil back above $100/barrel. Core CPI is seen at +0.2% MoM / +2.4% YoY. Tariff-driven inflation — particularly against Canada — is proving more persistent than initially assumed. Markets are pricing ~70% odds of a 25bps hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signaling more work needed on inflation. Trump is publicly pressuring the Fed to cut rates, while some economists argue a hike would serve as a statement of Fed independence.
